items.title: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain
items.summary: The crash, between a moving train and another that was stopped further up the track, was caused by an "inexplicable" error, the transport minister said.

confirmed_facts.text: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain - Published A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: High-speed train crash kills at least 68 people in Spain - Published A high-speed train crash has killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more in central Spain.

confirmed_facts.text: It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: It occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into another train - which was stationary on the tracks - on Wednesday morning.

confirmed_facts.text: The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the crash, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The transport minister said a computer failure followed by human error caused the crash, which is one of the worst in Europe's modern history, and Spain's deadliest train disaster in 13 years.

confirmed_facts.text: Survivors described harrowing scenes of passengers being thrown into the air, trapped in the wreckage and smashing windows to get out.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: Survivors described harrowing scenes of passengers being thrown into the air, trapped in the wreckage and smashing windows to get out.

confirmed_facts.text: The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, Spain's Transport Minister Ãscar Puente said.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: The stationary train, run by private rail operator Iryo, had 147 passengers on board, and had stopped on the tracks because of a computer failure, Spain's Transport Minister Ãscar Puente said.

confirmed_facts.text: He explained that when there is a system failure, a 24-hour control centre in Madrid takes over, but it had made an "inexplicable" decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions.

items.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
items.summary:
I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games.
